newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Swedish PM says joining EMU still an open question.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM says joining EMU still an open question.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Saturday the decision was still open on whether his country should join the EU's planned economic and monetary union (EMU).
Persson, speaking to reporters at an EU summit, said that if he asked Sweden's parliament or people today, they would say no.
"We have to decide next autumn and the decision is still open. Let's wait and see," Persson said.
Persson also told Reuters Financial Television that the most important decision during the summit was agreement on a pact to enforce fiscal discipline after EMU.
"Because without that, we would have lost momentum," Persson said, adding he believed Sweden "can live with it" if it were to join EMU.

But he also hinted that the final word may not yet been said on the stability pact. "You will have an ongoing discussion about EMU and the growth and stability pact...so what it will all look like in the end, I think it's too early to have an opinion."

Asked whether this meant the agreement was not necessarily the final word on how decisions would be taken on countries running excessive deficits, he said, "No, I'm not sure about that. But the process is still on track."
